biography.plain_text: King Albert II is Belgium’s former monarch and a son of King Leopold III. Before succeeding his brother Baudouin in 1993, he represented Belgian exporters on international trade missions and served as president of the Belgian Red Cross. He abdicated in 2013 in favour of his son Philippe, while retaining the title of King.

long_biography.plain_text:
King Albert II of Belgium spent part of his childhood in wartime displacement. The son of Leopold III and Queen Astrid, he and his siblings were deported with their father during the German occupation. After liberation, the royal children lived in Switzerland, where Albert continued his schooling. Decades later, he chaired a Council of Europe ministerial conference devoted to protecting cultural and architectural heritage.

His elder brother Baudouin's death brought Albert to the throne, where he swore the constitutional oath before parliament. During Belgium's prolonged coalition deadlock after the 2010 election, he consulted party leaders and appointed mediators. He met Elio Di Rupo at Laeken as negotiations continued across the country's linguistic divide.
long_biography.html:
King Albert II of Belgium spent part of his childhood in wartime displacement. The son of Leopold III and Queen Astrid, he and his siblings were deported with their father during the German occupation. After liberation, the royal children lived in Switzerland, where Albert continued his schooling. Decades later, he chaired a Council of Europe ministerial conference devoted to protecting cultural and architectural heritage.

His elder brother Baudouin's death brought Albert to the throne, where he swore the constitutional oath before parliament. During Belgium's prolonged coalition deadlock after the 2010 election, he consulted party leaders and appointed mediators. He met Elio Di Rupo at Laeken as negotiations continued across the country's linguistic divide.
